Microchip Technology.role: Broad-line supplier of microcontrollers and analog chips increasingly used in edge/embedded AI, but its highly cyclical, inventory-sensitive end markets (auto, industrial) recently emerging from a downturn temper its AI upside and durability.

ON Semiconductor.role: ON makes power management and silicon-carbide chips whose data-center power-delivery exposure is a growing but small slice of a business still dominated by cyclical auto/industrial end-markets, hence modest near-term growth and mid-tier moat.

GlobalFoundries.role: GlobalFoundries is a specialty foundry focused on differentiated mature/trailing-edge nodes for automotive, IoT, RF, and industrial markets; it sits in AI-infra but only peripherally, as it lacks leading-edge capacity and faces cyclical, capex-sensitive end demand with modest near-term growth.

United Microelectronics.role: UMC is a Taiwan-based pure-play foundry specializing in mature and specialty nodes (28nm and above); it sits in AI-infra as a supplier of power management, RF, and specialty chips, but its cyclical mature-node exposure and lack of leading-edge AI logic keep growth modest and moat moderate.

Entegris.role: Entegris supplies ultra-high-purity materials, filtration, and specialty chemicals essential to advanced chip fabrication; recurring consumable-driven demand gives it decent durability, but exposure to wafer-start cyclicality and fab capex keeps growth and elasticity moderate.

MKS Instruments.role: Supplies critical subsystems (vacuum, RF power, lasers, optics) for semiconductor fabrication and advanced packaging; benefits from AI-driven capex but is cyclical and carries elevated leverage from the Atotech acquisition.

Advanced Energy Industries.role: Supplies precision power conversion and control subsystems for semiconductor fabrication equipment and data-center infrastructure; a real AI-infra beneficiary but its demand is tied to cyclical WFE and capex spending, limiting durability and moat.

Cirrus Logic.role: Fabless supplier of mixed-signal and audio codecs heavily concentrated in Apple smartphones; modest single-digit growth and customer concentration make it a cyclical consumer-electronics play rather than a data-center AI beneficiary.

Lattice Semiconductor.role: Fabless leader in small/low-power FPGAs for edge, industrial, comms and client compute; recovering from an inventory-correction cycle with modest reacceleration, holding a strong niche moat but exposed to cyclical end-markets and only indirect AI leverage.

Allegro MicroSystems.role: Allegro makes magnetic-sensing and power ICs concentrated in automotive (EV/ADAS) and industrial markets; only tangentially AI-linked, it is a cyclical analog-semi play with solid niche share in Hall-effect sensors but exposure to auto and inventory cycles.

Power Integrations.role: Fabless supplier of high-voltage power conversion ICs for chargers, appliances, and industrial systems, with modest AI/data-center power exposure; flat TTM revenue and cyclical end-markets keep it a quality-mid cyclical rather than a secular AI winner.

Wolfspeed.role: Pure-play SiC substrate and power device maker for EV/industrial markets; heavy capex burn, negative earnings, balance-sheet stress and softening demand place it in speculative territory despite a credible long-term SiC TAM.

Skyworks Solutions.role: Supplies RF front-end modules for smartphones and IoT/connectivity devices; heavy Apple concentration and mobile-cycle exposure make revenue flat-to-declining and cyclical, with only tangential AI relevance, so it sits as a lower-quality cyclical semis name.

Qorvo.role: Qorvo supplies RF front-end modules heavily tied to smartphone cycles (notably Apple/Android), making it a cyclical mid-cap with modest AI exposure and concentration risk that caps moat and earnings durability.

Synopsys.role: Synopsys is a duopoly EDA vendor providing the design and verification tools essential to every advanced chip; recurring license revenue and mission-critical positioning make demand durable and largely non-discretionary, sitting in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels enabler.

Photronics.role: Photronics is a leading merchant maker of photomasks used in chip and display lithography; it sits as a cyclical AI-infra supplier with a decent duopoly-adjacent moat but flat revenue and capex-sensitive demand.

FormFactor.role: FormFactor supplies probe cards and test/measurement systems used in semiconductor wafer test; it benefits from HBM/advanced-packaging demand but sits in a cyclical, capex-sensitive test niche with moderate moat.

Cohu.role: Cohu supplies test handlers, contactors and consumables for semiconductor back-end test; it sits in AI-infra as a cyclical equipment name with modest recurring revenue but heavy exposure to volatile chip capex cycles.

UiPath.role: UiPath is a leading robotic process automation software vendor pivoting toward agentic AI; decelerating single-digit growth, competitive pressure from Microsoft, and discretionary IT spend exposure place it in the disruptive bucket with moderate moat and permanence risk.

BigBear.ai.role: Small-cap provider of AI-driven decision intelligence and analytics for defense/government customers; sits in disruptive because of tiny revenue, weak ~3% YoY growth, persistent unprofitability, and low moat against larger integrators, making it highly speculative despite sticky government contracts

Verint Systems.role: Verint provides customer-engagement and contact-center software increasingly repositioned around AI bots and analytics; flat revenue, mid-tier moat, and low valuation place it as a modest-growth AI-adjacent name rather than a secular winner.

Pegasystems.role: Enterprise low-code BPM and decisioning software vendor pivoting to AI-driven workflow automation; recurring subscription revenue supports durability but flat/declining top-line and mid-tier moat in a crowded market keep it a quality mid-cap rather than a secular leader.

Twilio.role: Cloud communications (CPaaS) provider adding AI-driven messaging and customer engagement; usage-based recurring revenue gives moderate durability but growth has decelerated to high-single-digits amid competition and pricing pressure.

DigitalOcean.role: Developer-focused cloud provider targeting SMBs with a nascent GPU (Paperspace) offering; sits as a smaller AI-platform player with modest growth, limited moat versus hyperscalers, and cyclical SMB exposure.

Fastly.role: Fastly runs an edge cloud/CDN platform for content delivery and edge compute, but slow ~5% growth, persistent unprofitability, customer concentration and intense competition from Cloudflare/Akamai/hyperscalers make it a speculative disruptive name with a weak moat.

Akamai Technologies.role: Mature CDN operator pivoting to edge security and compute; legacy delivery is decelerating (rev YoY ~1%) while security and cloud segments provide modest growth, placing it as a defensive, cash-generative name with limited AI-driven upside.

Equinix.role: Leading colocation/interconnection data center REIT with recurring lease revenue and dense network ecosystems; durable demand and high switching costs place it as a defensive AI-infra play, though REIT rate sensitivity and heavy capex temper multiples.

Digital Realty Trust.role: Global data center REIT leasing colocation and hyperscale capacity; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels landlord with recurring, contracted rental income that benefits from AI-driven demand but is capital-intensive and rate-sensitive.

Iron Mountain.role: Records-management REIT expanding into data-center colocation; its AI-relevant data-center segment is small relative to the legacy storage base, so exposure is real but diluted, with recurring contracted revenue lending durability.

Switch peer Cyxtera skip / Cologix N/A -.role: QTS (owned by AMT proxy here) provides data-center and communications-tower infrastructure with long-term leases; recurring contracted revenue and high switching costs make it a low-beta, capex-resilient digital infra REIT with only indirect AI upside.

Eaton.role: Diversified electrical equipment maker supplying power distribution, switchgear, and UPS gear to data centers; strong secular AI-power demand but sits in AI-infra with moderate cyclicality tied to construction capex cycles.

Quanta Services.role: Leading electric power and grid infrastructure services contractor benefiting from data-center-driven load growth and grid modernization; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels enabler but with cyclical capex exposure and moderate moat in a fragmented services market.

GE Vernova.role: Diversified power/grid equipment maker (gas turbines, grid, wind) benefiting from data-center power demand and grid buildout; sits in AI-infra as a picks-and-shovels electrification play, but earnings carry cyclicality and wind-segment drag that cap quality and durability.

Emerson Electric.role: Diversified industrial automation and process controls leader whose products support data-center power/cooling and factory automation; the AI-relevant slice is a portion of a slow-growing, cyclical but durable franchise, placing it in defensive with moderate capex sensitivity.

Generac Holdings.role: Leading maker of residential/commercial backup generators and energy storage; demand is tied to weather-driven outages and consumer discretionary spend, making it cyclical with only tangential AI/data-center power exposure.

Schneider peer Hubbell.role: Maker of utility and electrical infrastructure products (transmission/distribution grid components, connectors, enclosures) benefiting from grid modernization and data-center power buildout; sits in defensive due to steady but modestly-growing, utility-tied demand with moderate cyclicality.

Powell Industries.role: Powell makes custom electrical switchgear and power distribution systems for industrial, oil/gas, and increasingly data-center clients; it benefits indirectly from AI power buildout but is a cyclical, project-driven equipment maker with modest recent growth and no dominant moat.

Oklo.role: Pre-revenue developer of small modular fast reactors targeting data-center and industrial power; speculative long-duration bet with no deployed units, licensing/regulatory risk, and valuation entirely on future TAM rather than current earnings.

GE Aerospace peer / Curtiss skip - Ormat.role: Vertically-integrated geothermal developer/operator with long-life PPA-backed baseload assets and a product/energy-storage segment; recurring contracted power revenue and a durable renewable niche place it as a defensive infrastructure name rather than a high-growth AI play, with modest single-digit

Southern Company.role: Regulated electric utility in the Southeast benefiting from load growth tied to data-center buildout; sits defensive due to rate-based earnings, low beta, and non-discretionary demand, with only modest AI-linked upside.

Duke Energy.role: Regulated electric utility positioned to benefit from data-center/AI load growth in its Southeast service territory; earnings are rate-base-driven and durable, making it a defensive, low-beta indirect AI-power play rather than a growth name.

Dominion Energy.role: Regulated electric utility with strong data-center load growth in Virginia (Data Center Alley), providing durable but modest AI-adjacent upside via power demand rather than technology exposure.

MasTec.role: MasTec is a diversified infrastructure engineering/construction firm with power delivery, clean energy, and communications segments benefiting from grid buildout and data-center power demand; it sits as a cyclical AI-infra beneficiary with moderate moat and capex-sensitive project backlog.

EMCOR Group.role: Mechanical/electrical contractor benefiting from data center buildouts; solid execution but cyclical, project-based revenue tied to construction capex makes it vulnerable to a freeze.

Flex.role: Flex is a diversified electronics manufacturing services provider whose data-center and power/cooling segment benefits from AI buildout, but low-margin cyclical contract manufacturing with modest growth and fragmented competition places it as a moderate-quality AI-infra name.

Amkor Technology.role: Amkor is the largest US-based outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, benefiting from advanced packaging demand but sitting in a cyclical, capital-intensive, competitive market with modest growth and margins tied to fab utilization.

TTM Technologies.role: TTM makes printed circuit boards for aerospace/defense, data-center and networking end markets; it benefits from AI hardware buildout but remains a cyclical, capital-intensive component supplier with modest pricing power, hence mid-tier quality and elevated beta.

Vishay Intertechnology.role: Vishay makes commodity passive and discrete components (resistors, capacitors, diodes, MOSFETs) for broad industrial, auto, and electronics markets with modest AI-datacenter exposure; it sits as a low-growth, cyclical component supplier in a fragmented market with limited pricing power.

Kulicke and Soffa.role: KLIC makes wire-bonding and advanced packaging equipment for chip assembly; its highly cyclical, capex-driven revenue and modest scale place it as a volatile mid-tier AI-infra supplier with recovering but unproven durability.

ARKK (ARK Innovation).role: disruptive-innovation basket LED BY TESLA (~10%), then AMD, CRISPR, Tempus AI, Robinhood. High beta, rich multiples, Tesla-driven idiosyncratic swings — NOT a semis basket.

QQQ (Nasdaq-100).role: Nasdaq-100 mega-cap tech; quality, but rich and tech-tilted.

VOO (S&P 500).role: broad US large-cap; the market itself — durable, diversified.

SCHD (Dividend).role: quality-dividend value basket; low beta, cheap, durable earnings.

DTCR (Data Ctr Infra).role: data-center REITs & digital infra (Equinix, Digital Realty, American Tower); physical, contracted, durable — low beta.

GRID (Smart Grid).role: grid/power equipment for the AI electricity demand (Eaton, Quanta, GE Vernova); inelastic infra spend.

NUKE (Nuclear/Uranium).role: nuclear/uranium for data-center baseload (Constellation, Vistra, Cameco, BWX); high-growth but cyclical/volatile.
